name: How do I make an ADU feel like a luxury home instead of a tiny box?

mainEntity.name: How do I make an ADU feel like a luxury home instead of a tiny box in a high-end Los Angeles neighborhood?
mainEntity.text: How do I make an ADU feel like a luxury home instead of a tiny box in a high-end Los Angeles neighborhood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Luxury in an ADU is usually about proportion and experience, not just size. High ceilings, large well-placed windows, consistent flooring, and strong indoor-outdoor flow can make a compact unit feel generous. Built-in storage, a calm material palette, and a kitchen and bath that are simple but refined also help. The architecture should avoid awkward hallways and cramped corners, because those make even a large ADU feel smaller than it is. In upscale neighborhoods, the unit should also relate to the main residence through quality and character without copying it too closely. A well-designed ADU feels private, bright, and coherent. Homeowners should focus on the elements that occupants notice daily: light, layout, storage, and sound control. Those details matter more than decorative complexity.
acceptedAnswer.description: A luxury-feeling ADU comes from ceiling height, natural light, proportion, quality finishes, good storage, and a clear indoor-outdoor connection. A compact plan can still feel spacious when circulation is efficient and the architecture is clean and intentional.
